proposals.evidence: DEDR 2872 full article (p. 249) gives Kor. (O.) jōku , (T.) jēki to wash. Go. (Tr. W. Ph.) sōkānā to apply ointment, hot water, etc., to one's skin, rub, apply (oil, etc.); (SR.) mat sokānā to apply medicine, anoint; (G. Mu. S.) h Bhat jōku “to wash” matches Lindgren Koraga jōku “wash” in form and sense; this cross-source match is a candidate lead, with the full DEDR article defining the family. Both source identities and dialect tags are preserved.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 88 full article (p. 11) gives Kor. (T.) ḍakke areca nut. Bhat ḍakke “arecanut” is the same cited Koraga form and sense; its original dialect:Koraga:tappu:Tappu uncertain dialect tag is retained. The article is used as family classification, not an independent second attestation of Bhat.
